findings.problem: Replacing mismatched private canvas/source pictures can omit GPU-live retired textures from combined resident-byte accounting.
findings.scenario: Submit a partial job, cancel, start at a different canvas size before completion, cancel again, then admit an atlas transfer. wgpu retains the old submitted texture while atlas_resident_bytes charges only current replacement storage.

findings.suggestion: Track retired picture ownership/bytes by completion sequence and reap them after nonblocking completion service.

core_reasoning: ReachScan retains set/frame/partial reach across turns. Set headers and sprite identifiers each consume a visit; the same cell is retained until its reach resolves. Final cell inspection is separately charged. No repeated-prefix scan was found.
Missing/capped reach metadata continues to use a conservative viewport scissor. MAX_METADATA_VISITS and MAX_REACHES limit cached geometry, not accepted scenes or painter operations.
Each original instance completes all of its disjoint tiles before the cursor advances, preserving cell-major layer order, row direction, free-run order and final-only publication across yields.
PictureLedger keeps replaced private canvas/source/base resources and their byte charges until their recorded last-use completion. NeverSubmitted pictures can be dropped immediately.

Wider resources use the shared monotonic CompletionWindow sequence. Pending legacy retirement receives a callback only after controls_submitted confirms all older encoded work was submitted. Submitted live legacy pictures obtain a fence when actually retired.
Legacy tagging before resource replacement is conservative. Same-size reuse remains safe by queue ordering. No new CPU/GPU completion wait was found.
